what: The commands install_eo_cmd puts on a person's path. koine maintains these under role R35 in kanon's docs/roles.md -- their text, their options, and what they ask an assistant to do. What joining costs and what a member is held to is R4's and stays with the office: this repository maintains the program that states the rule and has no standing to change the rule.
history: Both were kanon's prompts/join_eo and prompts/init_eo until 2026-09-17, when kanon deleted them and R35 was created to hold them here. They were briefly stored as unmodifiable copies; that arrangement ended with the handover, and koine now writes them.

commands.name: eo_join
commands.what: join the Eunoia ecosystem, run inside the repository that is joining

commands.name: eo_init
commands.what: start a tool: write a README saying what it is for, complying with nothing

commands.name: eo_bump
commands.what: move a pinned dependency onto a commit whose CI is green, and refuse otherwise

commands.name: koine_append_db
commands.what: add a run's new bugs to the database of every bug a tool has found. For a person at a terminal: a pinned consumer resolves it through its own lock and must not take it off PATH, which would lose the pin

convention: Every installed command carries a prefix saying whose it is, because the name is claimed inside somebody else's process and on their PATH. `eo_` is the ecosystem's commands, which run inside a tree that is not this one. `koine_` is this repository's own. install_eo_cmd refuses anything else.
kinds: `prompt` hands context to an assistant and takes --show-prompt, which prints what it would hand one and runs nothing. `program` does the work itself.
